title: Incidence and risk stratification of perioperative atrial fibrillation
summary:
Background:
Irregular heart rhythms can occur after major surgery. One common type is new-onset atrial fibrillation around the time of surgery. This condition may increase the risk of stroke, heart attack, and death. However, the exact frequency of this complication after non-cardiac surgery is still unclear.

Research Question:
This study aims to determine how often atrial fibrillation occurs during or after non-cardiac surgery. It also seeks to identify which patients are at higher risk. In addition, the study will investigate whether affected patients have more cardiovascular complications in the long term.

Methods:
Approximately 1,000 patients aged 55 years or older undergoing planned surgery in thoracic surgery, general and abdominal surgery, vascular surgery, orthopedics, or urology will be included.
Before surgery, participants will undergo a structured medical assessment including blood testing. Continuous heart rhythm monitoring will be performed before, during, and for up to three days after surgery.
Depending on the time of enrollment, patients will be followed for up to five years to record the occurrence of atrial fibrillation, stroke, heart attack, hospitalizations, or death.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients undergoing surgery in the following specialist departments: thoracic surgery, general and visceral surgery, vascular surgery, orthopedics, and urology. 
•    Inclusion no more than 28 days and at least 18 hours before surgery.
•    Age ≥ 55 years.
•    Signed informed consent form available.
Exclusion criteria:
The exclusion criteria are defined as follows:
•    Pre-existing atrial fibrillation
•    Emergency surgical procedures
•    Patients incapable of giving consent
•    Patients who are hospitalized by court order or official order.
